newsitem.title: UK: No-fly zone can be patrolled without France - U.S..
newsitem.headline: No-fly zone can be patrolled without France - U.S..

text.p: U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher and British Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind agreed on Thursday that their two countries could if necessary patrol the extended no-fly zone in southern Iraq without French help.

"In discussions on the no-fly zone they agreed that no matter what the French do, the U.S and the UK have the capability to implement effectively the (expanded) no-fly zone," Nicholas Burns, U.S. State Department spokesman, told reporters.

Christopher is flying to Paris for talks with the French government after his meeting with Rifkind in London. The French have been cool in their attitude towards two U.S. missile attacks in southern Iraq this week.
"We've got sufficient air assets in the region to implement the extended no-fly zone," Burns told reporters travelling with Christopher.

Asked whether Iraqi leader Saddam Hussein had achieved his own victory in northern Iraq by reasserting control over his Kurdish territories, Burns said: "This won't be sustainable over the long term."
